answer: A proof-of-chemical-work scheme requires each agent to synthesize a photoluminescent pigment under randomized reaction parameters before registering. An automated spectrometer analyzes the emission signal to confirm correct stoichiometry. An adversary seeking to forge identities must expend tangible chemical precursors and energy per batch, rendering Sybil generation cost-prohibitive. However, precursor impurities can alter the spectral output, occasionally rejecting valid agents.
